Loaded bytes beyond the eight metatile attribute pages. The byte-indexed attributes end at $87FF and the engine’s indirect graphics sources address the bitmap, item texts, paths and sprite banks elsewhere. A redraw watch observed 1,024 attribute reads and zero reads in this range.

comments.text: Cycles through three timeslots and selects the two-byte target in the interrupt dispatch table.
Unsigned energy reservoir capped at $FF. Zero reached through damage sets the end flag.
Set by air underflow, fatal damage and the completed rescue sequence. Evaluated at the end of the main loop.
Row-major room ID used to select objects, enemies and room-specific rules.
Copy of the VIC sprite-sprite collision latch read by the main loop. Used by contact damage and item overlap tests.
Prevents a held trigger from repeating the inventory action until fire has been released.
Main playfield's colour value copied to the VIC's second shared sprite multicolour register.
High byte of the first working pointer, used for tile output positions and temporary inputs to frame copies.
High byte of the second zero-page data pointer used for surface copying and gauge frame loads.
Current tile byte passed from room map fetch to the per-tile drawing routine.
Room column times 16. Horizontal room transitions add or subtract $10.
Room row times eight. Vertical room transitions add or subtract $08.
Countdown for advancement of the moving player sprite frame index.
Set after Up input and during dive transitions. Nonzero delays automatic upward movement.
Low byte of the player's sprite X position. Horizontal movement keeps its ninth bit in the sprite X mask.
Vertical sprite position, updated by directional input and by buoyancy.
Packed ninth X bits for the sprites across the 256-pixel boundary.
Counts calls to the air routine before the next decrement of the remaining-air counter.
The low byte of the KERNAL RAM IRQ vector, set to $E9 by the game startup.
The high byte of the KERNAL vector. The game sets $41 and the driver's standalone prologue selects $91 instead.
Sprite slots $20 and $21 receive the two live Myrtle frames. Higher sprite slots in this bank hold other actor and panel graphics.
Sprite slot $22 is used by sprite 4 in the HUD, at X $30 and Y $3E.
First energy-gauge buffer copied by $533C and selected by HUD sprite 3 with pointer $23.
VIC sprite pointers $33–$35 address these HUD graphics slots.
The second of two sprite buffers refreshed together by the energy-gauge routine.
Frame buffer loaded for Gordon and the two fixed-position puzzle actors. The playfield uses sprite pointer $37 for it.
Second frame buffer for Gordon. Selected with pointer $38 in the playfield.
A 128-tile-wide map with 32 rows. Each $80-byte row contains eight 16-tile-wide room slices. The redraw selects eight successive rows of one slice.
Start of the second band of eight metatile rows. The room above/below handlers change the start address by $0400.
Start of the map's third room row. The initial map also seeds passage tiles patched by dynamite during play.
Three consecutive map tile IDs cleared by the dynamite patch at $5AA3.
Three map tile IDs cleared at $5A9C when the room $14 blast applies its patch.
Start of the deepest room row, including the rooms with the rescue barrier and item-triggered patches.
Destination for the first five tiles of the room $1E state update.
Five metatiles one map row after the first row of the room $1E patch.
Three metatiles at the right edge of the second metatile row modified by the room $1E update.
First three-tile row cleared by the room $1C dynamite patch.
Three metatiles directly below the right-hand room $1E patch.
Second three-tile row cleared under the room $1C passage.
Three map tile IDs cleared when the rescue starts, restored from $5AC8 at reset.
Eight-byte HUD glyphs at screen codes $00–$3F. The alphabet sits at $01–$1A, space at $20 and the digits at $30–$39.
Ten eight-byte glyphs for the panel edges and junctions, indexed by screen codes $40–$49.
Last pair of the panel border characters, including the lower junction.
Four 64-byte creature frames. The raster handler adds the animation index to pointer $8C.
The eleven-item lookup maps onto an eight-slot object frame bank at pointer $90 plus the mapped frame number. Several inventory items share a silhouette.
Last eight cells of the bitmap row behind the HUD before the bitmap display is enabled.
Two authored 40-cell bitmap rows across the top of the room frame. The room redraw starts one row below this band.
Right border pixels of row 6 and the left border pixels of row 7. The linear bitmap stores these two outer edges consecutively.

Right border pixels of the final room row, immediately before the full-width lower band.
Two authored 40-cell bitmap rows below the room rectangle, containing the bottom border.
Installs hardware state once before entering the restart path. The unpacker transfers control here.
Clears the attempt's state and presents the title before entering the main loop.
Waits for raster line 200, checks controls, advances actors and items, runs room events and checks for an end of play.
Banks out BASIC, selects the HUD glyphs, puts sprites behind foreground bitmap pixels, and installs the IRQ.
Clears the main working state while preserving facing, rebuilds the HUD and item tables, initializes the air and energy gauges, and waits for fire on the title screen.
Sets all 1000 screen cells to $0C and clears the corresponding colour RAM.
Installs the KERNAL RAM vector at $0314, enables the raster IRQ on line 0 and clears the CIA timer A interrupt mask.
Acknowledges the VIC interrupt and dispatches through a JMP operand updated by the previous raster handler. Other IRQs return through the saved KERNAL stack frame.
Low byte of the JMP operand written by the raster phase dispatcher.
High byte of the active raster dispatch target.
Walks the three-entry handler table and rewrites the IRQ dispatch JMP operand before returning.
Three little-endian dispatch targets for raster lines 0, 90 and 180.
Indexed high-byte view of the raster table. The IRQ dispatcher doubles the phase index before reading it.
Selects character mode and configures the panel sprites and black background. Schedules the playfield handler at line 90.
Sets the playfield's video mode and colours, programs actor sprites, samples collisions and ticks the sound driver when enabled.
Sets the final band's background colour and schedules the next frame's line 0 interrupt.
Toggles $444C on a newly pressed CIA1 port B bit 4 and clears its latch when the bit is released.
Index of the item assigned to sprite 5, with $80 indicating an empty slot.
Index of the item assigned to sprite 7, with the same $80 empty value.
One live countdown flag per dynamite index. Item pickup tests this flag before accepting the item.
Room in which each dynamite charge is armed, compared with the displayed room on detonation.
Three fuse counters initialized to $C8 when the respective item lands.
Alternates its low bit so Gordon's trajectory index advances on alternate loop passes.
Item index for the inventory. A negative byte means the carry slot is empty.
Remaining air. Its high nibble drives the air gauge and decrementing zero ends the attempt.
Two active movement masks copied from the current room creature script and shifted to test four directions.
Packed-decimal percentage shown in the first line of the HUD.
Four bytes marking which of the 32 rooms have already earned a first-visit point.
Sound toggle flag tested by the raster handler before calling the SID driver.
Packed-decimal high score displayed on the second line of the panel.
Even-spaced low and high offsets for the left edge of bitmap cells.
High-byte view of the indexed bitmap column offset table.
High byte of the final directly accessible column-offset pair and the additional pairs beyond the 32-column room window.
Row pointers for writes to screen RAM and, after adding $D400, the corresponding colour RAM.
High-byte view of the interleaved row table used by the screen attribute writes.
Low address bytes in $20 steps, selected by the low three bits of a tile ID.
Bitmap source page $60 plus the tile ID divided by eight.
Counts down a pending music change and writes request 2 to $9000 on expiry.
Splits a tile index into bitmap-source page and offset, copies two strips of pixels and supplies four screen and colour attributes. Dark rooms zero the attributes instead.
Low operand of the first 16-byte metatile read, patched using the three low bits of the tile code.
High operand of the first strip source, loaded from the tile code divided by eight.
Low operand of the first bitmap strip write.
High operand of the upper strip write, patched using the character row and column offsets.
Low operand of the second strip read, calculated by adding 16 to the first source address.
High byte of the second strip source, adjusted for carry from the low byte.
Low operand byte of the lower bitmap-strip write, advanced by the 320-byte row stride.
High operand byte of the second bitmap-strip store. The renderer recalculates it from the first strip's address.
Rooms $14 and $1C are dark unless item 9 is carried or appears in either visible room item slot.
Computes room index and redraws eight rows of 16 metatiles from $1000 plus the room's map offset, then installs the room's actors and colours.
Low operand byte of the indexed metatile row read, advanced by $80 each tile row.
High operand byte of the room map read. Written from the map position and advanced along with its low byte once per tile row.
Copies one 64-byte frame for the special actor in room $0C or $1E to $0DC0.
Low destination operand for the selected 64-byte actor frame.
High byte of the destination operand. Set by Gordon's alternate two-sprite frame and the end animation, restored before room drawing.
Four offsets for the actor animation's 64-byte source alignment.
Selects one of the $9A–$9F source pages for the fixed actor and ending animation sprite frames.
Advances the room $0C actor's animation, awarding eight points on its completed sequence when the room trigger is armed.
Once armed in room $1E, advances its animation, reveals item 6, adds eight points and queues sound request 10.
Moves one map row up where there is a row above. On reaching row zero, requests music 2 if the delayed-music counter is zero.
Moves one map row down where there is a row below. On entering row 1, requests music 4 if the delayed-music counter is zero.
Subtracts one column from the room map offset unless already at the leftmost column.
Adds one column to the room map offset unless already at the rightmost column.
Gates movement by mode and lock flags, reads the four active-low direction bits from CIA1 port A, and dispatches vertical and horizontal movement.
Consumes up, down, left and right in sequence. Vertical motion updates the Y byte and horizontal motion updates X and its high bit.
Handles a right-hand room edge and updates the room coordinates before redrawing when crossing is permitted.
Moves Myrtle to a fixed entry position, switches to mode 4, resets the frame index and queues music request zero.
Tests the left edge before subtracting from X and handles the room transition where allowed.
Tests the lower Y boundary and calls the lower-room transition at the boundary.
Tests the upper Y boundary and calls the upper-room transition when crossed.
Converts the player's working coordinates to sprite positions and ninth X bits for the raster handler.
Copies two 64-byte Myrtle frames from the source bank into the live sprite buffers at $0800 and $0840.
Low source operand and output of the generic sprite frame-pointer calculation.
High source operand and output of the same calculator, indexed by frame ID divided by four.
Low operand byte of the player frame copy. The driver advances it by $40 for the second sprite.
High operand byte of the sprite copy target, used with $49FD to advance from the first destination to the second one.
Four byte offsets for 64-byte aligned frames within each page.
Sprite source page $A0 plus the frame ID divided by four, for frame indices 0 through 127.
Selects a four-frame range from the player's facing flag, copies the frame pair and steps the cycle when the countdown expires.
Selects movement and animation according to the opening, jump, swim and surface modes.
Selects the player's directional frame set before the next sprite update.
If the recorded collision bit and a local bitmap probe both indicate obstruction, sets the corresponding bit in the active-low direction mask.
Converts the test object's 9-bit X and 8-bit Y into character-cell coordinates used by collision probes.
Samples bitmap strips around Myrtle. Direction selects the relative cells and whether the probe tests 16 contiguous bytes or two eight-byte strips.
Low operand patched for the eight-byte bitmap probe.
High operand byte of the eight-byte bitmap sample. The routine advances the address to sample a second screen row.
Low operand for the 16-byte bitmap cell sample.
High byte patched before the 16-byte adjacent-cell probe.
In swim mode, waits out the recent Up input delay. When buoyancy is active, passes two synthetic Up inputs through the terrain filter and movement code.
Four masks that select the collision bits before each directional terrain probe.
One bit per primary direction. The terrain check ORs it into the active-low input to block that direction.
Frame-by-frame heights shared by the launch and dive sequences.
Polls the VIC raster register until it reads $C8, synchronizing the main loop with the display.
Looks up the bitmap offset for the working cell row and column and returns the summed pointer in $47 and $48.
Four repeating low bytes for consecutive 320-byte bitmap row strides.
High bytes for the row addresses used by the character-cell bitmap probes.
Loads the current room's creature slots from the coordinate and movement tables.
Initializes sprite 4 coordinates, flags, colour, path pointer and path index for the room.
Reads sprite 6 coordinates from the room tables and initializes the enable bit, colour, timer and path index from constants.
Reads duration and direction pairs for active creatures, loops when the flags byte is $FF, applies one-pixel movement and advances the four-frame animation index.
Advances the room $1A animation and removes the creature with an eight-point award when it reaches the required object position.
Four values copied into the creature frame mask operand during the room $1A animation.
Programs expanded sprite 2 at a fixed position for rooms $0C and $1E.
Masks for the ninth X bit of sprites 4 and 6.
Programs positions, colours, pointers and enable bits for the creatures in VIC sprites 4 and 6.
Sprite colour lookup indexed by the one-based creature type.
Operand changed by the room $1A actor routine before the frame-selection logic.
Selects a four-frame group by creature and horizontal direction and copies 256 bytes into its sprite display bank.
Low source operand patched from the selected creature frame index.
High operand of the creature graphics source, copied from the sprite lookup result.
Low byte of the destination byte stream selected for creature slot 0 or 1.
High byte of the dynamically selected frame bank destination.
Low bytes $40 and $00 of the two 256-byte live sprite frame banks.
High bytes $0E and $23 of the two live creature graphics banks.
Adds one packed-decimal point per count in Y and redraws the score and high score display.
Splits packed-decimal score and high score into digit glyphs and writes the numbers and percent signs into the upper panel.
Screen code for the percent marker drawn after each BCD field.
Steps the panel heart frame after its countdown and uses the room-dependent delay between animation loops.
Fills three bytes of the room bitset with successive random bits and masks out bit 6 in its last byte.
Tests the current room's stout bit and fills the bottle sprite coordinates and flags when it is set.
Uses the room bottle slot to update its sprite during the playfield raster handler.
With a visible bottle and a qualifying sprite overlap, fire removes the bottle from its room bitset, adds $20 energy capped at $FF and redraws the gauge.
Detects item 10 assigned to room $19, clears three map cells, locks movement, and starts the rescue track with eight points.
Applies motion flags and delays from a two-byte record stream in room $19. The terminator sets the completion and end flags.
Flag and delay pairs for the rescue animation, ended by $FF in the flag position.
Second byte of each rescue record, reloaded into the motion timer on each flag change.
Four bytes recording which rooms have a bottle available.
Bitset byte covering rooms $18–$1F. The randomizer clears bit 6 after generating it.
Eight masks used with the room number's low three bits in the room-state bitsets.
Low X coordinate of a bottle, used when the room's bottle bit is set.
Bottle Y coordinate by room, loaded with its matching X table entry.
Converts the remaining-air high nibble to the clockwise needle frame selector by subtracting it from $35.
On prescaler expiry, reloads $C0 and decrements the air byte. For a nonnegative result it recalculates the gauge frame. Underflow sets the pending end flag.
Uses a fire latch on CIA1 port A bit 4 to call the pickup path when empty-handed, or place the held object in one of two free room slots.
Return instruction between the drop routine's tail jump and the adjacent inventory label routine.
Uses the held item index to select a text pointer and length, converts letters to screen codes and writes the inventory label.
Blanks the eight cells reserved for the held object name.
Copies $37 bytes from the initial object data to the mutable item table at the start of an attempt.
Reads the VIC sprite collision latch, filters sprite combinations and deducts energy for qualifying contact.
Uses the high three energy bits to select two 64-byte bottle frames and copies them into the panel sprite buffers.
Converts a frame index into the low and high bytes of a 64-byte frame address through separate lookup tables.
Tests the pending end flag, runs the ending animation and delay, then discards its return address and restarts.
Starts at heart frame 3 and uses its extended animation until frame 7 before proceeding to the end scene.
Clears both display override flags, then falls through to the line-200 delay.
Repeats the line-200 wait 150 times.
Polls active-low fire on joystick port 2 until pressed.
Walks and animates Gordon in the opening, follows the dive trajectory, then manages his sprite frames in room $19.
Zeros the promenade frame index, then falls through to copy the corresponding pair of sprite frames.
Adds two to Gordon's X low byte, setting his sprites' ninth X bits on overflow.
Positions and enables Gordon's two sprites. Uses vertical or horizontal placement depending on the current animation.
Samples the raster counter for the two bytes subsequently updated by the random-state routine.
Rotates the two seed bytes and mixes them with exclusive-or and add before saving the new low byte.
Selects the heart timing and a room-dependent display colour from the map position after the opening phase.
Divides the horizontal tile offset by 16 and adds the vertical map offset to get the row-major room index.
Sets the room's bit in the four-byte visited table and adds one percentage point if the bit was clear.
Scans eleven item records for the current room and assigns at most two present items to the live sprite slots.
Programs sprites 5 and 7 from the room object slots, leaving the VIC sprite-enable bits in place for other sprites.
Applies alternating vertical displacement in the surface row during swim mode, with exceptions for rooms $03 and $04.
Initializes the delay, step and direction state for the surface bob after a room redraw.
Changes the room sprite Y coordinate of item 8 in small alternating steps when its room is at the surface.
Selects an overlapping item slot from the collision bits, rejects lit dynamite and clears the selected item's present bit as the item becomes held.
Advances falling items and the rising chest, checks bitmap surfaces or coordinate stops, then calls room-specific landing handlers.
Tests a falling object's position and the presence of item 7 in either live slot before arming the room $1E event.
Advances a sinking item down one row where possible. The chest moves up one row instead.
Tests two adjacent character cells on the same bitmap scanline near a settling item. Returns carry set for a blocked sample unless the surface exception applies.
Requires object 0 present and a specific three-sprite overlap in room $1F, then clears a room flag, hides sprite 6 and awards eight points.
In room $1E while carrying item 6, tests both present slots for item 5 to choose the eight-plus-one-point branch or the alternate room state.
Checks the settling item's X window and tests whether item 6 is visible and marked in motion. Arms the room $0C actor and clears item 6's present bit on success.
Checks the player's coordinates against a rectangle in room $0C and repeats the standard contact damage path while the actor is enabled.
Copies two slices of authored tile data into the map area for the room $1E state change.
Loads the initial source offset before rewriting the room $1E tile patch at reset.
Restores the three saved map tile IDs at the four passage locations affected by dynamite.
Clears three metatiles at $184B when the room $14 dynamite patch runs.
Clears three tile bytes beginning at $1801. The blast code selects this patch by rewriting its own call target.
Clears two rows of three metatiles at $1DC6 and $1E46 when the room $1C patch runs.
Copies three initial tile IDs back into the rescue room's movable barrier.
Three initial map tile indices for the barrier at $1F17.
Records the room and starts a $C8-pass timer when item 1, 2 or 3 finishes falling.
Counts three fuse timers down, removes each detonated item, starts the shake, kills the player in the blast room and applies the passage change when the room matches its table.
Low operand of the JSR selected from the blast-specific passage patch table.
High operand of the JSR dynamically patched from the three dynamite-specific map update addresses.

Stores three random bits briefly while the shake routine combines them with VIC control register 2.
Three tile codes copied into each destructible passage at reset.
Room IDs $1C, $14 and $10 for the three dynamite items.
